extracted.intended_audience: state air agencies and other entities preparing CAA section 111(d) state plans under these EPA emission guidelines
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and evaluation criteria for state plan submissions implementing EPA's emission guidelines for affected electric generating units (EGUs) under CAA section 111(d). Covers plan components, completeness criteria, compliance flexibilities (rate- and mass-based), monitoring/reporting, and meaningful engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent level of emission reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans must ensure an equivalent level of emission reduction from the sources that are affected sources under these emission guidelines. States cannot rely on or account for emission reductions occurring at non-affected sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans must demonstrate that they achieve the level of emission reduction that would result if each affected source were individually achieving its presumptive standard of performance (after accounting for any application of RULOF). See sections X.B and X.D.1 for discussions of stringency and demonstrating equivalence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumptively approvable unit-specific mass-based compliance (long-term coal-fired subcategory)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is finalizing a presumptively approvable unit-specific mass-based compliance approach for units in the long-term coal-fired subcategory that includes a backstop rate to ensure an equivalent level of emission reduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States should consider EPA discussions of stringency and demonstrating equivalence and guidance on particular compliance flexibilities when deviating from the presumptively approvable method or for sources without a presumptively approvable approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowing mass-based emission trading (medium- and long-term coal-fired subcategories) with conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: States may include mass-based emission trading for affected coal-fired EGUs in the medium- and long-term subcategories, but EPA requires use of a unit-specific backstop rate and a demonstration that the program achieves an equivalent level of emission reduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA will not provide a presumptively approvable mass-based trading approach due to heightened risks in calculating mass budgets and uncertainty in utilization assumptions; states choosing mass-based trading must demonstrate equivalence and satisfy the same caveats that apply to unit-specific mass-based compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mass budget establishment and allowance distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: To establish a mass budget under these emission guidelines, states would use the rate-based standard of performance and an assumed level of utilization for each participating affected EGU, sum individual mass limits to an aggregate mass budget, and specify how allowances would be distributed to participating affected EGUs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each allowance represents a tradable permit to emit one ton of CO2; affected EGUs must surrender allowances based on reported CO2 emissions; total emissions from participating EGUs should be no greater than the total mass budget; each participating EGU must also demonstrate compliance with the unit-specific backstop rate.

rubrics_metrics.name: High scrutiny of utilization assumptions in mass-based programs
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA will apply a high degree of scrutiny to assumptions about the utilization of affected EGUs participating in a mass-based trading program in state plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because projecting utilization is increasingly challenging (changes in technology, fuel prices, electricity demand), assumptions must be documented and conservative where necessary; an improper assumption for one EGU can implicate others in a trading pool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation of mass limit calculations and assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: States must demonstrate how the mass limit has been calculated and the basis for any assumptions (e.g., about utilization) when proposing mass-based compliance approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must specify the structure and purpose of any other trading program design feature(s) (e.g., mass budget adjustment mechanism) and how they impact the demonstration of an equivalent level of emission reduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures and systems for emission averaging/trading implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: If states elect to incorporate emission averaging or trading (rate- or mass-based), they must establish procedures and systems necessary to implement and enforce the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes mechanics for demonstrating compliance (e.g., surrender of compliance instruments based on monitoring and reporting of CO2 emissions and generation), establishing continuous monitoring and reporting requirements, and developing a tracking system for tradable compliance instruments. EPA may provide technical support and allow use of EPA infrastructure (e.g., allowance management system) where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling differing compliance dates in trading/averaging
rubrics_metrics.description: States incorporating emission averaging or trading must consider differing compliance dates for affected EGUs given variation by subcategory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The most straightforward approach supported by commenters is to initially include only sources with a compliance date of January 1, 2030, and add sources into the program at the start of the first year in which their standard applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance banking considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: States must consider whether to provide for banking of tradable compliance instruments; allowance banking may provide incentives for earlier reductions and liquidity but can create long-term surpluses that undermine program stringency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unrestricted banking may result in allowance surpluses; states should consider restricting banking or including recalibration mechanisms (e.g., annual allowance bank recalibration) to prevent surpluses and ensure continued calibration toward equivalent stringency.

rubrics_metrics.name: State plan development timeline (24 months)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is finalizing a 24-month state plan development timeframe for submission of state plans under these emission guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA believes 24 months is reasonable given fewer sources covered and restrictions on certain compliance flexibilities; the presumptively approvable approach for unit-specific mass-based compliance for long-term coal-fired subcategory may simplify plan development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interstate emission trading requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: States may incorporate interstate emission trading (rate- or mass-based) into their plans but must address stringency and logistical concerns and demonstrate equivalence for all participating affected EGUs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interstate programs require all participating states to use the same form of trading, have consistent design elements and identical trading program requirements. Each state submits its own plan (coordinated to address the interstate trading program). EPA needs all state plan submissions that incorporate interstate trading before evaluating any individual plans; EPA can provide technical assistance but coordination across EPA regions may be necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-use of reductions from non-affected sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Emission reductions from sources not affected by this rule cannot be used to demonstrate compliance with a standard of performance established to meet the emission guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only emission reductions at affected EGUs may count towards compliance with the state plan, including toward demonstrating equivalence of compliance flexibilities. States may account for existing state programs only as they apply to the same affected EGUs included in the plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative completeness criteria (subpart Ba)
rubrics_metrics.description: State plan submissions must meet the administrative completeness criteria listed in 40 CFR part 60, subpart Ba.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete list: (1) formal letter of submittal from the Governor or designee; (2) evidence the state has adopted the plan in state code/regulations or issued the document in final form (including adoption/issuance date and effective date); (3) evidence the state has necessary legal authority; (4) copy of the actual regulation/document to be incorporated, including indication of changes (redline/strikethrough) and an exact duplicate electronic copy, with publication cover page/table of contents if applicable; (5) evidence the state followed all applicable procedural requirements; (6) evidence public notice consistent with 40 CFR 60.23a, including date; (7) certification that public hearing(s) were held consistent with notice and state law; (8) compilation of public comments and the state's response; (9) documentation of meaningful engagement (list of pertinent stakeholders, summary of engagement, summary of stakeholder input, description of how input was considered).

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical completeness criteria (subpart Ba)
rubrics_metrics.description: All plans must meet technical criteria under subpart Ba.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical criteria include: (1) description of the plan approach and geographic scope; (2) identification of each designated facility (affected EGU), standards of performance for each affected EGU, and monitoring/recordkeeping/reporting requirements to determine compliance; (3) identification of compliance schedules and/or increments of progress; (4) demonstration that the state plan submission is projected to achieve emission performance under the applicable emission guidelines; (5) documentation of state recordkeeping and reporting requirements to determine plan performance; (6) demonstration that each standard is quantifiable, permanent, verifiable, enforceable, and non-duplicative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required characteristics of standards of performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards of performance must be quantifiable, verifiable, permanent, enforceable, non-duplicative, and continuous in nature (per CAA section 302(l)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless expressly amended, subpart Ba provisions apply. States must express standards in specified units and ensure they meet these characteristics in plan regulations and implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of each affected EGU and subcategory assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans must identify each affected EGU and the subcategory to which each affected EGU is assigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identification should be clear and used consistently throughout the plan, including in calculations of baselines, standards of performance, and any compliance flexibility application.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of coal-fired EGUs planning permanent cessation (by Jan 1, 2032)
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans must include, in the regulatory portion of the plan, a list of coal-fired steam-generating EGUs that are existing sources at the time of submission and that plan to permanently cease operation before January 1, 2032, and the calendar dates by which they have committed to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan must provide that an EGU operating past the date listed is no longer exempt and is in violation of the plan, except to the extent the EGU has a time-limited extension pursuant to the reliability assurance mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Units and expression of standards of performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards of performance must be expressed in lb CO2/MWh gross basis or, for affected EGUs in the low load natural gas- and oil-fired subcategory, lb CO2/MMBtu, or, if a state allows mass-based compliance, tons CO2 per year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must specify the units used and ensure consistency with monitoring and reporting systems to enable enforcement and EPA review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline emission performance data and selection of 8 continuous quarters
rubrics_metrics.description: For each affected EGU, state plans must identify baseline emission performance using CO2 mass and electricity generation data (or heat input for certain low-load subcategories) from 40 CFR part 75 reporting for the 5-year period immediately prior to publication, and identify which continuous 8-quarter period from that 5-year period was used to calculate baseline emission performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must include the data and indicate the chosen 8-quarter period; data sources and selection rationale must be documented for EPA replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation requirements when using compliance flexibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a state plan provides for the use of a compliance flexibility (alternative standard form, emissions averaging, or trading), the plan must identify the presumptive unit-specific rate-based standard that would apply absent the flexibility; the standard actually applied; how it is calculated; provisions for implementation and enforcement; identification of the unit-specific backstop emission limitation for mass-based flexibilities; and a demonstration the plan will achieve an equivalent level of emission reduction to individual rate-based standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans must provide sufficient methods, assumptions, and calculations for EPA to review and determine whether the flexibility achieves equivalent or better emission reduction and to replicate the state's calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increments of progress and enforceable reporting obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans must include increments of progress and reporting obligations and milestones as enforceable elements for affected EGUs within applicable subcategories or pursuant to consideration of RULOF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These requirements must be clearly stated in the enforceable regulatory portion of the plan and include timelines and reporting formats sufficient for EPA and stakeholders to determine compliance progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforceable commitment to permanently cease (medium-term and RULOF reliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: For affected EGUs in the medium-term coal-fired subcategory and EGUs relying on a plan to permanently cease operation for a less stringent standard pursuant to RULOF, the state plan must include an enforceable commitment to permanently cease operation by a date certain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The plan must clearly identify calendar dates for cessation commitments; operations past the committed date may render the source non-exempt and in violation unless a time-limited extension applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that existing coal-fired EGUs operate only subject to standard or exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans must provide that any existing coal-fired steam generating EGU shall operate only subject to a standard of performance pursuant to these emission guidelines or under an exemption from applicability provided under 40 CFR 60.5850b.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes any time-limited extensions of cessation dates pursuant to the reliability assurance mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring, reporting, and recordkeeping (MRR) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans must include monitoring, reporting, and recordkeeping requirements for affected EGUs sufficient to determine compliance with standards of performance and program obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MRR should align with 40 CFR part 75 data sources where applicable and provide the basis for allowance surrender, compliance demonstrations, and EPA review and enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data/documentation sufficiency and replicability for EPA review
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans must adequately document and support the process and underlying data used to establish standards of performance and any compliance flexibilities, including CO2 mass emissions and corresponding electricity generation or heat input data, and identify the period used to determine unit-specific baselines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must include data and documentation sufficient for EPA to understand and replicate calculations, including methods, assumptions, and calculations necessary to review plans containing compliance flexibilities and to determine equivalence; plans must demonstrate transparent and verifiable implementation and enforcement measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaningful engagement requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: States must conduct meaningful engagement in the plan development or revision process: 'timely engagement with pertinent stakeholders and/or their representatives in the plan development or plan revision process.' Pertinent stakeholders include industry, small businesses, and communities most affected by and/or vulnerable to impacts of the plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engagement should not be disproportionate in favor of certain stakeholders and should be informed by best practices. States should recognize and engage communities most affected or vulnerable and tailor engagement to local conditions; documentation of meaningful engagement (list of stakeholders, summary of engagement, summary of input, description of how input was considered) is required as part of administrative completeness.
